holidays.name: National Proofreading Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the people who catch the typos, stray commas and embarrassing autocorrects before the rest of the world sees them. Reread that email, menu or text one more time.
holidays.origin: Founded by author and writing teacher Judy Beaver, who created it to encourage care and accuracy in written work. It is an unofficial observance and has been marked on March 8 for years.
holidays.funFact: Typos have caused some very expensive mistakes. A missing hyphen in a 1960s code for NASA's Mariner 1 probe is often blamed for its failed launch, though historians still debate the details.

holidays.name: National Peanut Cluster Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy clumps of crunchy peanuts coated in chocolate. They are easy to make at home with only a few ingredients, and a good excuse to eat candy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its exact origin is unclear. It has a regular place on the March 8 calendar of candy holidays.
holidays.funFact: Peanuts are not true nuts. They are legumes that grow underground, so a peanut cluster is technically a chocolate-covered bean treat.

holidays.name: National Middle Name Pride Day
holidays.description: A day for people to show some love for the middle name that usually only gets used when they're in trouble. Share it, explain it, or bring it out for the occasion.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed among the quirky holidays on March 8.
holidays.funFact: Many people in the U.S. have a middle name, and it's often a family surname or the name of a relative.
